newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end higher as JGBs rise, stocks fall.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end higher as JGBs rise, stocks fall.

text.p: The key June three-month deposit rate contract ended higher on Monday due to a rise in Japanese government bond futures and a fall in Tokyo share prices.
A city bank trader said the rise was probably due to short-covering triggered by a fall in Tokyo share prices and a rise in JGBs.
In the Tokyo stock market, the key Nikkei 225 average ended down 133.36 points at 20,796.37.
The key December JGB futures contract ended at 125.32, up sharply from Friday's 124.70.
A trust bank trader said the June Euroyen futures contract may also have been pushed up by a fall in interest rate swap (IRS) rates.
The three-year IRS rate was quoted at 1.29/1.33 percent as of 0706 GMT, down from 1.31/1.35 percent late on Friday.
Turnover of the June Euroyen futures contract during Monday's day session was 31,758 contracts.
Comments by Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan have had little effect on the market, traders said.
Greenspan declined to comment on interest rates or currencies in his remarks to the Federation of Bankers Associations of Japan.
Greenspan is in Tokyo for meetings with Japanese financial and monetary authorities.
Traders said the key overnight call rate was traded at 0.47 percent on Monday.
They said the Bank of Japan is likely to maintain its neutral money market stance at least until the release of the central bank's key 'tankan' corporate sentiment survey on November 27.
No new key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued on Monday. Three-month CDs were tagged with a sell qoute of 0.51 percent.
About 20 billion yen worth of one-month CDs was issued at 0.49 percent, a trader for another city bank said.
Two-month CDs were tagged with a sell quote of 0.50 percent. All CD rates were unchanged from Friday.
